name: Raman spectra of naturally aged edible oils, Data Set 1A: the 2016 LBNL campaign (Gilbraith et al., Applied Spectroscopy Practica 2025)
description: 99 Raman spectra of naturally aged (5-7 year) edible oil bottles, Data Set 1A (the 2016 LBNL campaign of Gilbraith et al. 2025): one spectrum per bottle, 100 deposited rows for the 100 purchased bottles, of which one (class 15) is an all-NaN placeholder the authors replaced with NaN to keep the matrix rectangular (excluded here). Peroxide-value regression: the primary target is the peroxide value (PV, by wet-chemical titration) of each bottle (1.5-165.4, no missing values); the oil class is also recorded in the CSV, so a classification task is derivable, but the coverage is unbalanced (class 1: 27 spectra down to single-spectrum classes) and class 4 (avocado oil) is absent while class 20 (3 spectra) has no name in the deposit's 19-entry class key. Native 1,340-point spectra over -18.1-1,974.2 cm^-1 (~1.1-2.0 cm^-1 spacing) stored as the CSV column headers (one shared axis) and used as is, so no resampling is involved; the low-wavenumber end is negative, an instrument export artifact retained as deposited. Intensities are raw counts (2.8e4-2.1e7, arbitrary units); instrument model and excitation wavelength are not recorded in the deposit. Oils are commercial bottles from grocery stores in and around Newark, Delaware (2014-2016), aged naturally for 5-7 years. The CSV is served from a frozen copy mirrored at HTW-KI-Werkstatt/RamanBench (aged_oils/, size + sha256 pinned; the live Mendeley download sits behind a WAF that 403s non-browser clients, hence the mirror).

rai:dataCollection: Raman measurements (one spectrum per bottle) of 100 naturally aged edible oil bottles (99 loaded), 2016 campaign; peroxide values by wet-chemical titration. Instrument model and excitation wavelength are not recorded in the deposit.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: None in the loader. The CSV is the deposit's analysis-ready export; intensities are raw as deposited. The authors' supplemental R code applies its own preprocessing in analysis, not to the deposited data.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The per-spectrum peroxide value (wet-chemical titration) and the oil class (from the commercial product) are recorded in the deposit's CSV; no human labelling of the spectra themselves was involved.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No personal or sensitive information is included. All samples are commercial edible oils without any human identifiers.
rai:dataBiases: Single 2016 lab campaign (LBNL) on oils naturally aged 5-7 years from one 2014-2016 purchasing window in one region (Newark, Delaware), so class and PV distributions may not represent other regions, seasons, brands or aging periods. Class coverage is unbalanced (class 1: 27 spectra down to single-spectrum classes 11, 14, 16, 18, 19) and class 4 is absent while class 20 (3 spectra) has no name in the deposit's 19-entry class key. One row is an all-NaN placeholder (excluded). The low-wavenumber end of the axis is negative (instrument export artifact, retained as deposited). 99 spectra is a small set for a 19-class classification.
rai:dataLimitations: 99 spectra; 19 oil classes with unbalanced and partly unnamed coverage (class 20 unnamed, class 4 absent); one all-NaN placeholder row excluded; negative wavenumbers at the low axis end (kept as deposited); instrument and excitation wavelength not recorded; the 2019 repeat campaign (Data Set 1B) was deposited only for NIR, so cross-year Raman generalisation with this probe is not possible.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Supports research into shelf-life and freshness assessment of edible oils (food safety and quality); any consumer- or regulatory-facing use requires validation against independent lots, brands and aging conditions.
rai:dataUseCases: Peroxide-value (freshness) regression from a single Raman spectrum; oil-class classification (19 classes, with the coverage caveats above). Group-aware splitting is not applicable (one spectrum per bottle).
prov:wasGeneratedBy: Data collection: Raman spectra of naturally aged (5-7 year) edible oil bottles purchased from grocery stores in and around Newark, Delaware between the summer of 2014 and the spring of 2016 (Gilbraith, Carter, Adams, Sota-Uba, Lavine, Booksh & Ottaway, Applied Spectroscopy Practica 3(2) 2025, doi:10.1177/27551857251340426; Mendeley Data deposit ctgg7k4m5g v2, doi:10.17632/ctgg7k4m5g.2, CC BY 4.0). Data Set 1A is the 2016 Raman campaign (Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory), one spectrum per bottle, with the peroxide value (PV) of each bottle by wet-chemical titration. 99 spectra are loaded (the deposit's 100th row, a class-15 sample, is an all-NaN placeholder the authors used to keep the matrix rectangular and is excluded). 19 oil types per the deposit's class key; this file carries classes 1-3 and 5-20 (class 4, avocado oil, absent; class 20, 3 spectra, unnamed in the 19-entry key). Native 1,340-point axis -18.1-1,974.2 cm^-1 (CSV column headers, used as is; the low end is negative, an instrument export artifact retained as deposited); raw counts 2.8e4-2.1e7. The CSV is served from a frozen copy mirrored at HTW-KI-Werkstatt/RamanBench (aged_oils/, size + sha256 pinned) because the live Mendeley download sits behind a WAF that 403s non-browser clients.
